long_biography.plain_text:
The Honan family acquired a small flour mill in central-west New South Wales in 1952, when Dick Honan was still a child. His later leadership turned that inherited base into a broader manufacturing group. A pivotal move came in 1970, when he led the purchase of a starch plant at Nowra, establishing a platform for expansion into specialised food and industrial ingredients.

Honan remains chairman, while the next generation handles managing-director and board duties. The group now processes wheat, sugarcane and canola into flour, starches, gluten, alcohol, oils and stockfeed. Its ownership is family-wide: Honan was historically identified as a principal shareholder, but no current personal percentage is public. Company factories, revenues and the separately named Manildra Foundation therefore should not be treated as his individual assets.
